chunks: And Abān narrated from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a camel that fell into a well and was slaughtered from the side of its tail. He said: “There is no harm in it if they mentioned the name of Allah over it.”

key_terms.اسْمَ اللَّهِ: the name of Allah, whose mention is required over the animal
key_terms.بَعِيرٍ: a camel, the animal under discussion in the ruling
key_terms.بِئْرٍ: a well, the location creating necessity in the slaughter method
key_terms.تَرَدَّى: fell down, indicating the animal plunged into the well
key_terms.ذَنَبِهِ: its tail, indicating the side from which the slaughter was performed
key_terms.ذُبِحَ: was slaughtered, referring to the act of ritual killing
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm, a formula indicating permissibility

ai.seo_question: Is a camel that fell into a well lawful to eat if it was slaughtered from the side of its tail?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning an animal that became inaccessible in a well and was slaughtered in an unusual manner. The Imam عليه السلام states that there is no harm in it, provided that the name of Allah is mentioned over the animal at the time of slaughter.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4167 - Aban narrated from Zurara, from Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), who said:

I asked Imam (as) about a camel that fell into a well and was slaughtered from the side of its tail.
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm in it if they mentioned the name of Allah (swt) over it."
